title: Apple TV 4K Gets Screen Saver Shuffle, Sign Language Support in tvOS 27.2
text:
Apple TV 4K Gets Screen Saver Shuffle, Sign Language Support in tvOS 27.2 — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Apple TV 4K Gets Screen Saver Shuffle, Sign Language Support in tvOS 27.2
 Add preferred source 1 Apple will release tvOS 27.2 next week, adding three features to the Apple TV 4K. A new Shuffle option lets the device rotate through all screen saver categories instead of locking users into one. The Apple TV app gains sign language toggles in the player controls for selected titles, with both American and British Sign Language confirmed in the third beta. Users can also manually select which photos from an iPhone or iPad appear in Memories & Slideshows and Portraits screen savers. Separately, the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K arrives November 13 with Siri AI and a four-speaker HomePod surround setup, while a larger HomeView hub with a robotic arm is reportedly in development for 2027 or later. Key Elements 
 Apple Apple TV 4K tvOS 27.2 Apple TV app HomePod Siri Sigmund Judge Mark Gurman HomeView Apple is set to push out tvOS 27.2 next week, a software update that brings three additions to the Apple TV 4K: a screen saver shuffle mode, sign language options inside the Apple TV app, and finer control over custom photo screen savers.
 The release candidate build is already available, with the public rollout expected within days.
 The most visible change is the new Shuffle option for screen savers. Until now, Apple TV owners had to pick a single category - Aerials, Memories & Slideshows, Portraits or Snoopy - which meant the others never appeared. With the update, the device can rotate through every available screen saver category over the course of a day.
 Accessibility gets a boost as well. For selected movies and shows that carry the relevant tracks, the Apple TV app now offers a sign language toggle directly in the player controls. Sigmund Judge reported that the third beta of tvOS 27.2 confirmed both American Sign Language and British Sign Language would be supported.
 The third feature gives users more control over Photos-based screen savers. When configuring the Memories & Slideshows or Portraits categories, they can now hand-pick which images from an iPhone or iPad are included, rather than granting the Apple TV access to the entire photo library.
 Separately, Apple is preparing hardware changes for its living-room lineup. The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, due November 13, will ship with support for Siri AI and a new four-speaker HomePod surround sound configuration. Siri AI is also headed to the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K, though it is not part of tvOS 27.2.
 Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has reported that Apple is developing a larger, premium version of its HomeView smart home hub fitted with a motorized robotic arm. The arm, mounted on a base, could rotate a full 360 degrees and use voice recognition to point the speaker toward whoever is speaking. The device is expected to carry a 9-inch display, larger than the current model, and has been assigned the internal codename J595. Gurman put the launch target at 2027 or 2028, with the final name either entirely new or a suffix such as Max or Ultra. Talk of a robotic-arm HomeView has circulated for several years, with earlier projections pointing to a 2026 or 2027 release at roughly $1,000.
 For Apple TV owners, the software update is a low-friction upgrade that adds polish rather than new hardware requirements. The shuffle feature in particular addresses a long-standing limitation of the platform's well-regarded aerial footage, which users previously had to choose at the expense of other categories.
 The sign language addition puts Apple's set-top box closer to the accessibility features already standard on its phones and tablets, and could matter for content partners whose libraries include ASL and BSL tracks. The photo selection tool also reduces the privacy trade-off for users who want personal images on their televisions but are reluctant to expose an entire library.
 Apple has not disclosed how many titles currently offer sign language tracks, and availability will vary by region and studio.
